docs.title: KGCL: Knowledge Graph Change Language
docs.text:
The Knowledge Graph Change Language (KGCL) is a standard for describing changes to ontologies and knowledge graphs (KGs). It describes changes at a high level, the way curators and ontology editors think about them: rename this term, add a synonym, move this class under a different parent, obsolete this term and point to its replacement.

rename UBERON:0002398 from 'manus' to 'hand'
create exact synonym 'cell nucleus' for GO:0005634
obsolete GO:9999999 with replacement GO:0005634

Source

Portions of this page, and Figures 2 and 3, are adapted from Hegde et al., A change language for ontologies and knowledge graphs, Database (2025), used under the CC BY 4.0 license. See Citing KGCL.

docs.title: Why a change language?
docs.text:
Ontologies and KGs are never finished. Terms are added, merged, and obsoleted; labels, definitions, and synonyms are corrected; and relationships are refined as knowledge improves. The Gene Ontology, for example, is more than 20 years old, and it still changes in every release.

Despite this, there has been no single agreed-upon way to represent or communicate those changes. That gap shows up in two places:

  • Retrospective changes ("diffs"). How do you tell people what changed between two releases? Comparing ontology O1 with O2 should produce the most parsimonious set of changes that turns one into the other. In the figure below, that is a single move of node E from under C to under B.
  • Prospective changes ("patches"). How do you ask for a change you want? Applying a change to O1 produces O2. Today, change requests usually arrive as free-text GitHub issues, which an ontology editor then has to translate by hand into edits in a tool such as Protégé.

The logic of ontology changes. (a) A diff between O1 and O2 yields a change object, here a NodeMove. (b) Applying that change object to O1 yields O2. Reproduced from Hegde et al. 2025, Fig. 2 (CC BY 4.0).

A low-level diff of OWL axioms is precise, but it doesn't match how editors think about changes: the move above would show up as one deleted axiom and one added axiom. In a 2023 community survey, 82% of ontology users said staying informed about changes was very or extremely important, yet only 8% were satisfied with the existing ways of viewing them. KGCL provides the higher-level representation that was missing.

docs.title: The three parts of KGCL
docs.text:
The components of KGCL. (a) A classification of change types, (b) a controlled natural language (CNL) for writing changes, and (c) a data model that serializes directly to formats such as YAML. Reproduced from Hegde et al. 2025, Fig. 3 (CC BY 4.0).
  1. A classification of change types. Changes that affect terms (nodes) and changes that affect relationships (edges) form two branches of one hierarchy. For example, NodeRename is a kind of NodeChange, alongside NodeCreation and NodeDeletion. Browse it in the class hierarchy, or see each type drawn out in the visual guide.
  2. A controlled natural language (CNL). A restricted subset of English that people can read and write, and that machines can parse without ambiguity: rename ENVO:01000575 from 'wax' to 'oil'. The CNL is defined by a Lark grammar.
  3. A data model. Each change type has a defined set of attributes. Every change has an id; a NodeRename also has about_node, old_value, and new_value. The model is written in LinkML, so the same change can be written as the CNL, JSON, YAML, or RDF, or as a table in a spreadsheet (less expressive).

The same rename in two of those forms:

CNLYAML 
rename ENVO:01000575 from 'wax' to 'oil'

id: CHANGE:001
type: NodeRename
about_node: ENVO:01000575
old_value: wax
new_value: oil

docs.title: Tools that use KGCL
docs.text:
Tool What it does with KGCL Ontobot GitHub Action that reads KGCL commands from an issue and opens a pull request that applies them to the ontology BioPortal Web forms that let curators propose changes without writing KGCL; BioPortal writes the KGCL and files the issue for Ontobot Ontology Access Kit (OAK) Python library and command line: diff two ontologies into KGCL, or apply KGCL to an ontology KGCL-Java and its ROBOT plugin Java parser and serializer, and a robot apply command for use in ROBOT pipelines This repository (kgcl-schema on PyPI) The schema, the generated Python data model, and the CNL parser and renderer

Not every tool supports every change type yet.

docs.title: Using the parser
docs.text:
pip install kgcl-schema
kgcl-parse "create exact synonym 'cell nucleus' for GO:0005634"

From Python:

from kgcl_schema.grammar.parser import parse_statement
from kgcl_schema.grammar.render_operations import render

change = parse_statement("add label 'nucleus' to GO:0005634")
type(change).__name__   # 'NewLabel'
render(change)          # "add label 'nucleus' to GO:0005634"

docs.title: Persistent URIs
docs.text:
These URIs resolve to the KGCL standard:

  • JSON-LD context: https://w3id.org/kgcl/kgcl.context.jsonld
  • OWL: https://w3id.org/kgcl/kgcl.owl.ttl
  • SHACL: https://w3id.org/kgcl/kgcl.shacl.ttl
  • YAML (LinkML schema): https://w3id.org/kgcl/kgcl.yaml

The KGCL classification is also browsable on BioPortal.

    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: dcterms:creator
    owner: AddNodeToSubset
    domain_of:

    range: string

    name: change_date
    description: The date and time at which the change was made
    comments:
    - In PROV terms, this is the time at which the activity that generated the change
      ended, i.e. the composition of 'was generated by' and 'ended at time'. It is
      stored directly on the change as a single value for convenience.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: dcterms:date
    owner: AddNodeToSubset
    domain_of:
    - Change
    range: datetime
  contributor:
    name: contributor
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: dcterms:creator
    owner: AddNodeToSubset
    domain_of:
    - Change
    range: string
  has_undo:
    name: has_undo
    description: A change that reverses this change
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    domain: Change
    owner: AddNodeToSubset
    domain_of:
    - Change
    - ChangeMixin
    range: Change
    multivalued: false
  change_description:
    name: change_description
    description: A string serialization of the change. This should be both human-readable,
      and parseable.
    comments:
    - '{''Form 1'': ''IRIs are denoted by CURIEs, optionally followed by label in
      parenthesis''}'
    - '{''Form 2'': "IRIs are denoted by the rdfs:label in single quotes, e.g. ''nervous
      system''"}'
    examples:
    - value: rename UBERON:0002398 from 'manus' to 'hand'
    - value: move 'hand' from 'part of' 'hindlimb' to 'part of' 'forelimb'
    - value: merge 'cellular metabolic process' into 'metabolic process'
    - value: search and replace 'metabolic process' with 'metabolism' in all labels
        under 'biological process'
    - value: search and replace 'metabolic process' with 'metabolism' in all labels
        under 'biological process' retaining as 'exact synonym'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    owner: AddNodeToSubset
    domain_of:
    - Change
    range: string
  associated_change_set:
    name: associated_change_set
    description: 'All changes forced as a result of this obsoletion. For example,
      starting with `A subClassOf B subClassOf C`, if we obsolete node B, then we
      may decide to bundle in a node move change of A from B to C. Note: this change
      set is not considered a part of the obsoletion, as obsoletion is considered
      atomic/simple. Instead this is a reference to a change set that may exist elsewhere'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    is_a: change_set
    owner: AddNodeToSubset
    domain_of:
    - Change
    range: Change
    multivalued: true
    inlined: true
    inlined_as_list: true
  in_subset:
    name: in_subset
    description: subset that the element is being placed inside.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    owner: AddNodeToSubset
    domain_of:
    - SubsetMembershipChange
    range: OntologySubset
  about:
    name: about
    description: The 'focus' entity on which the change operates
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    owner: AddNodeToSubset
    domain_of:
    - ChangeMixin
    range: OntologyElement
    multivalued: false

docs.title: Class: Edge
docs.text:
A relationship between two nodes.

Currently the only kinds of edges supported in KGCL:

__

_ * A subClassOf B <==> Edge(subject=A, predicate=owl:subClassOf, object=B)_

_ * A subClassOf P some B <==> Edge(subject=A, predicate=P, object=B)_

_ * P subPropertyOf Q <==> Edge(subject=P, predicate=owl:subPropertyOf, object=Q)_

__

These represent the most common kind of pairwise relationship between classes, and classes are the dominant node type in ontologies.

In future a wider variety of OWL axiom types will be supportedn through the use of an additional edge property/slot to indicate the interpretation of the axiom, following owlstar (https://github.com/cmungall/owlstar).

For example:

_ * A subClassOf R only B <==> Edge(subject=A, predicate=P, object=B, interpretation=AllOnly)_

_ * A Annotation(P,B) <==> Edge(subject=A, predicate=P, object=B, interpretation=annotationAssertion)_

__

Note that not all axioms are intended to map to edges. Axioms/triples where the object is a literal would be represented as node properties. Complex OWL axioms involving nesting would have their own dedicated construct, or may be represented generically. These are out of scope for the current version of KGCL

      parenthesis''}'

    domain_of:

    range: string

    name: associated_change_set
    description: 'All changes forced as a result of this obsoletion. For example,
      starting with `A subClassOf B subClassOf C`, if we obsolete node B, then we
      may decide to bundle in a node move change of A from B to C. Note: this change
      set is not considered a part of the obsoletion, as obsoletion is considered
      atomic/simple. Instead this is a reference to a change set that may exist elsewhere'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    is_a: change_set
    owner: EdgeCreation
    domain_of:
    - Change
    range: Change
    multivalued: true
    inlined: true
    inlined_as_list: true
  about:
    name: about
    description: The 'focus' entity on which the change operates
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    owner: EdgeCreation
    domain_of:
    - ChangeMixin
    range: OntologyElement
    multivalued: false

    rank: 1000
    owner: NodeMetadataAssertionChange
    domain_of:
    - Change
    range: string
  creator:
    name: creator
    comments:
    - This should be the composition of 'was generated by' and 'was associated with'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: dcterms:creator
    owner: NodeMetadataAssertionChange
    domain_of:
    - Change
    range: string
  change_date:
    name: change_date
    description: The date and time at which the change was made
    comments:
    - In PROV terms, this is the time at which the activity that generated the change
      ended, i.e. the composition of 'was generated by' and 'ended at time'. It is
      stored directly on the change as a single value for convenience.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: dcterms:date
    owner: NodeMetadataAssertionChange
    domain_of:
    - Change
    range: datetime
  contributor:
    name: contributor
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: dcterms:creator
    owner: NodeMetadataAssertionChange
    domain_of:
    - Change
    range: string
  has_undo:
    name: has_undo
    description: A change that reverses this change
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    domain: Change
    owner: NodeMetadataAssertionChange
    domain_of:
    - Change
    - ChangeMixin
    range: Change
    multivalued: false
  change_description:
    name: change_description
    description: A string serialization of the change. This should be both human-readable,
      and parseable.
    comments:
    - '{''Form 1'': ''IRIs are denoted by CURIEs, optionally followed by label in
      parenthesis''}'
    - '{''Form 2'': "IRIs are denoted by the rdfs:label in single quotes, e.g. ''nervous
      system''"}'
    examples:
    - value: rename UBERON:0002398 from 'manus' to 'hand'
    - value: move 'hand' from 'part of' 'hindlimb' to 'part of' 'forelimb'
    - value: merge 'cellular metabolic process' into 'metabolic process'
    - value: search and replace 'metabolic process' with 'metabolism' in all labels
        under 'biological process'
    - value: search and replace 'metabolic process' with 'metabolism' in all labels
        under 'biological process' retaining as 'exact synonym'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    owner: NodeMetadataAssertionChange
    domain_of:
    - Change
    range: string
  associated_change_set:
    name: associated_change_set
    description: 'All changes forced as a result of this obsoletion. For example,
      starting with `A subClassOf B subClassOf C`, if we obsolete node B, then we
      may decide to bundle in a node move change of A from B to C. Note: this change
      set is not considered a part of the obsoletion, as obsoletion is considered
      atomic/simple. Instead this is a reference to a change set that may exist elsewhere'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    is_a: change_set
    owner: NodeMetadataAssertionChange
    domain_of:
    - Change
    range: Change
    multivalued: true
    inlined: true
    inlined_as_list: true

docs.text: Obsoletion of a node deprecates usage of that node, but does not delete it.

docs.text:
name: NodeObsoletion
description: Obsoletion of a node deprecates usage of that node, but does not delete
  it.
from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
see_also:
- http://wiki.geneontology.org/index.php/Obsoleting_an_Existing_Ontology_Term
aliases:
- node deprecation
- class obsoletion
- term obsoletion
- concept obsoletion
is_a: NodeChange
mixins:
- Obsoletion
slot_usage:
  change_description:
    name: change_description
    string_serialization: obsoleting {about_node}
  associated_change_set:
    name: associated_change_set
    description: 'All changes forced as a result of this obsoletion. For example,
      starting with `A subClassOf B subClassOf C`, if we obsolete node B, then we
      may decide to bundle in a node move change of A from B to C. Note: this change
      set is not considered a part of the obsoletion, as obsoletion is considered
      atomic/simple. Instead this is a reference to a change set that may exist elsewhere'
    is_a: change_set
attributes:
  has_direct_replacement:
    name: has_direct_replacement
    description: An obsoletion replacement where it IS valid to automatically update
      annotations/edges pointing at the node with its direct replacement
    comments:
    - if a node obsoletion C, C about N1, and C has direct replacement N2, and there
      exists an edge with an edge property referencing N1, it is possible to replace
      with N2
    - if a node obsoletion C C about N1, and Chas direct replacement N2, then N1 IAO:0100001
      N2
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    close_mappings:
    - IAO:0100001
    rank: 1000
    owner: NodeObsoletion
    domain_of:
    - NodeObsoletion
    - NodeUnobsoletion
    range: Node
    multivalued: false
  has_nondirect_replacement:
    name: has_nondirect_replacement
    description: An obsoletion replacement where it is NOT valid to automatically
      update annotations/edges pointing at the node with its direct replacement

      exists an edge with an edge property referencing N1, it is possible to replace
      with N2
    - if a node obsoletion C C about N1, and Chas direct replacement N2, then N1 oio:consider

    domain: Change

    domain_of:
    - Change
    - ChangeMixin
    range: Deletion
    multivalued: false

    name: change_description
    description: A string serialization of the change. This should be both human-readable,
      and parseable.
    comments:
    - '{''Form 1'': ''IRIs are denoted by CURIEs, optionally followed by label in
      parenthesis''}'
    - '{''Form 2'': "IRIs are denoted by the rdfs:label in single quotes, e.g. ''nervous
      system''"}'

    name: associated_change_set
    description: 'All changes forced as a result of this obsoletion. For example,

    rank: 1000
    owner: ObjectPropertyCreation
    domain_of:
    - ChangeMixin
    range: OntologyElement
    multivalued: false

name: Obsoletion
description: Obsoletion of an element deprecates usage of that element, but does not
  delete that element.
comments:
- In OWL, deprecation is handled by the deprecation axiom. In OBO, we use this, but
  place additional requirements and expectations on obsolete elements

- http://wiki.geneontology.org/index.php/Obsoleting_an_Existing_Ontology_Term
- https://mondo.readthedocs.io/en/latest/editors-guide/merging-and-obsoleting/

- deprecation
- retiring

    - IAO:0000233
    rank: 1000
    owner: RemoveTextDefinition
    domain_of:
    - Change
    range: string

    name: creator
    comments:
    - This should be the composition of 'was generated by' and 'was associated with'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: dcterms:creator
    owner: RemoveTextDefinition
    domain_of:
    - Change
    range: string
  change_date:
    name: change_date
    description: The date and time at which the change was made
    comments:
    - In PROV terms, this is the time at which the activity that generated the change
      ended, i.e. the composition of 'was generated by' and 'ended at time'. It is
      stored directly on the change as a single value for convenience.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: dcterms:date
    owner: RemoveTextDefinition
    domain_of:
    - Change
    range: datetime
  contributor:
    name: contributor
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: dcterms:creator
    owner: RemoveTextDefinition
    domain_of:
    - Change
    range: string
  has_undo:
    name: has_undo
    description: A change that reverses this change
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    domain: Change
    owner: RemoveTextDefinition
    domain_of:
    - Change
    - ChangeMixin
    range: Change
    multivalued: false
  change_description:
    name: change_description
    description: A string serialization of the change. This should be both human-readable,
      and parseable.
    comments:
    - '{''Form 1'': ''IRIs are denoted by CURIEs, optionally followed by label in
      parenthesis''}'
    - '{''Form 2'': "IRIs are denoted by the rdfs:label in single quotes, e.g. ''nervous
      system''"}'
    examples:
    - value: rename UBERON:0002398 from 'manus' to 'hand'
    - value: move 'hand' from 'part of' 'hindlimb' to 'part of' 'forelimb'
    - value: merge 'cellular metabolic process' into 'metabolic process'
    - value: search and replace 'metabolic process' with 'metabolism' in all labels
        under 'biological process'
    - value: search and replace 'metabolic process' with 'metabolism' in all labels
        under 'biological process' retaining as 'exact synonym'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    owner: RemoveTextDefinition
    domain_of:
    - Change
    range: string
  associated_change_set:
    name: associated_change_set
    description: 'All changes forced as a result of this obsoletion. For example,
      starting with `A subClassOf B subClassOf C`, if we obsolete node B, then we
      may decide to bundle in a node move change of A from B to C. Note: this change
      set is not considered a part of the obsoletion, as obsoletion is considered
      atomic/simple. Instead this is a reference to a change set that may exist elsewhere'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/kgcl
    rank: 1000
    is_a: change_set
    owner: RemoveTextDefinition
    domain_of:
    - Change
    range: Change
    multivalued: true
    inlined: true
    inlined_as_list: true

docs.title: BioPortal: requesting changes without writing KGCL
docs.text:
BioPortal is a widely used portal for browsing biomedical ontologies. In BioPortal we leverage the KGCL standard to provide an easy workflow for users to request ontology changes. When users browse ontology classes, they now have access to a set of web forms in the user interface that allows them to enter information about their proposed change. The following figure shows a web form to request the addition of a synonym to the ‘cortical blindness’ class in the Mondo Disease Ontology (Mondo):

Providing web forms enables users to file a change request proposal without needing to know the particulars of the KGCL command syntax. Each web form presented to users has the necessary fields to collect data that is specific to the various change types, e.g., for the addition of a synonym the user will have a dropdown field that allows them to specify the type of synonym such as exact, narrow, broad, or related.

When users submit change request proposals via web forms, BioPortal collects the data and generates content for issues that are sent to GitHub in the repository where the ontology source file is maintained. The issues have human readable titles, and the body contents hold a machine-processable string that precisely describes the requested change as a KGCL command. Since a good deal of text across these issues is common, we used Ruby’s ERB templating system to build templates for each change request type. A GitHub issue title template for adding a synonym to a class appears as such in the BioPortal codebase:

Proposal: add synonym '<%= synonym_label %>' for <%= concept_label %>

After form submission the template is evaluated at runtime and the appropriate fields are dynamically replaced to create the human readable version:

Proposal: add synonym ‘cortical visual impairment’ for cortical blindness

The following figure shows the auto-generated body of the GitHub issue where a user requested the addition of “cortical visual impairment” as a synonym of “cortical blindness” in the Mondo ontology. BioPortal translated this change request to the machine-processable KGCL “create exact synonym” command:

Auto-generating issues from BioPortal with KGCL commands in the body allows complementary software such as Ontobot to detect these commands and programmatically implement the requested changes. This in turn saves ontology maintainers time, as they no longer have to implement the requested changes manually.

In order to generate GitHub issues from BioPortal, we make use of the GraphQL Client Ruby library for composing and executing GraphQL queries. This library allows us to interact with GitHub’s GraphQL API to look up repositories where ontology maintainers indicate their ontologies are housed, and programmatically create issues. Assuming an issue is successfully generated, GitHub’s GraphQL API returns the issue ID, and BioPortal displays a success message to users with a hyperlink that allows them to easily navigate to and view the issue page in GitHub:

BioPortal supports four KGCL change request types:

  • Synonym creation
  • Synonym removal
  • Class obsoletion
  • Class renaming

Change requests are switched on per ontology, since not every ontology's source files are kept on GitHub. As of the KGCL paper (2025), they were enabled for Mondo, GO, ENVO, and Uberon.

docs.title: Visual guide to change types
docs.text:
Each section below shows a small piece of an ontology before and after a KGCL change, followed by the KGCL command that makes the change. Changed elements are highlighted. Arrows point from a term to its parent: solid arrows are is_a (rdfs:subClassOf) and dashed arrows are other relationships, such as part_of (BFO:0000050).

The examples use real terms from the Gene Ontology and Uberon, but the edits are illustrations, not changes anyone has requested. For the full list of command forms and their YAML serializations, see Command examples. For every change type in the model, see the class hierarchy or the schema reference.

docs.title: Obsolete a term and name its replacement: NodeObsoletionWithDirectReplacement
docs.text:
Obsoletion marks a term as no longer to be used, without deleting it, so existing annotations that use the term can still be interpreted. Naming a replacement lets those annotations be updated automatically. Here, GO:9999999 stands for an accidental duplicate of nucleus.

flowchart LR
  subgraph before [Before]
    direction BT
    i1["GO:9999999<br/>cell nucleus"]
    i2["GO:0043231<br/>intracellular<br/>membrane-bounded organelle"]
    i3["GO:0005634<br/>nucleus"]
    i1 -- "is_a" --> i2
    i3 -- "is_a" --> i2
  end
  subgraph after [After]
    direction BT
    i4["GO:9999999<br/>obsolete cell nucleus"]:::changed
    i5["GO:0043231<br/>intracellular<br/>membrane-bounded organelle"]
    i6["GO:0005634<br/>nucleus"]
    i6 -- "is_a" --> i5
    i4 -. "replaced by" .-> i6
  end
  before ==> after
  classDef changed fill:#fff3b0,stroke:#b58900,stroke-width:2px
  linkStyle 3 stroke:#b58900,stroke-width:3px
obsolete GO:9999999 with replacement GO:0005634

Without a replacement: obsolete GO:9999999. To reverse an obsoletion: unobsolete GO:9999999.

Note

Exactly how an obsoletion is carried out (for example, prefixing the label with "obsolete", removing the term's parent relationships, or adding a term replaced by annotation) depends on the ontology's obsoletion policy and on the tool applying the change. The diagram shows a common OBO-style result.

docs.title: Creating and deleting terms
docs.text:
These change the set of terms rather than a term's content, so they have no diagram.

Change type Command ClassCreation create GO:9999999 NodeCreation (with a label) create node GO:9999999 'cell nucleus' NodeDeletion delete GO:9999999

Deleting a term removes it entirely. In most published ontologies, obsoletion is preferred, because other resources may already refer to the term.

docs.text:
Every KGCL change type sits in one classification hierarchy. Changes to terms (NodeChange) and changes to relationships (EdgeChange) are the two main branches under SimpleChange. The tree is regenerated from the schema each time the documentation is built.

docs.title: Ontobot: applying KGCL from GitHub issues
docs.text:
Many ontologies are developed on GitHub: change requests arrive as issues, and changes are made through pull requests (PRs). Turning each request into an edit by hand is slow, and it depends on an ontology editor having time to do it. Ontobot (the ontobot-change-agent) automates the middle of that process. It reads KGCL commands from an issue and opens a PR that makes the change. A curator still reviews and approves every PR.

Ontobot runs as a GitHub Action, so an ontology repository can add it without any other infrastructure. Repositories that use it include GO, Mondo, Uberon, ENVO, the Cell Ontology, and PATO; see the Ontobot README for the current list.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Ontobot watches new and edited issues for the phrase Hey ontobot!, apply: (the ! is optional), followed by a bulleted list of KGCL commands:

Hey ontobot!, apply:

- create exact synonym 'cortical visual impairment' for MONDO:0001385
- create related synonym 'CVI' for MONDO:0001385

A change request handled by Ontobot. (1) A user opens an issue in the ontology repository containing Hey ontobot!, apply: and a KGCL command, here adding an exact synonym to a Mondo term. (2) Ontobot sees the instruction and responds. (3) Ontobot opens a PR that makes the change in the ontology source file, and curators are assigned to review it. (4) Once a curator approves, the PR is merged and the change appears in the next release. Reproduced from Hegde et al. 2025, Fig. 4 (CC BY 4.0).

docs.title: Close-up: the issue and the pull request
docs.text:
An issue asking Ontobot to add a synonym to a Mondo term:

The change in the PR that Ontobot opens in response:

If a maintainer is satisfied with the change, they approve the PR and it is merged into the ontology source file. Otherwise they can edit it or close it, like any other PR.

docs.title: Setting it up
docs.text:
The Ontobot manual covers installation and provides a workflow template (.github/workflows/ontobot.yaml) to customize and add to the repository that holds the ontology source file.

Curators who would rather not write KGCL at all can request changes through BioPortal, which writes the KGCL and opens the issue for them.
